standard_prerequisites.name: Effective Cartier divisors on a regular surface over a discrete valuation ring
standard_prerequisites.statement: A regular model of a smooth curve over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring is a regular scheme of dimension two, flat and proper over the ring, with a special fibre that is a divisor supported on finitely many irreducible curves; an effective Cartier divisor on such a scheme is cut out locally by a single nonzerodivisor, and a divisor supported on one irreducible component is Cartier when the local ring at its generic point is a discrete valuation ring. A torsion-free module over a Dedekind domain is flat, and a scheme-theoretic cycle may be associated to a closed subscheme of the expected codimension. The author's own notions and the results of the Divisors, Chow and More on Algebra chapters that the proof quotes are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the divisorial description of the special fibre that the chapter uses everywhere afterwards, for instance when it attaches an invertible sheaf to the special fibre and when it speaks of degrees on the components.

core_obligations: Cut out the special fibre by a principal equation: the uniformizer of the discrete valuation ring gives an element of the structure sheaf of the model whose zero scheme is the special fibre, and since the model is flat over the ring and the element is a nonzerodivisor, the special fibre is an effective Cartier divisor (source lines 4561-4575).

Show that each component is Cartier: at the generic point of a component the local ring is a discrete valuation ring, so the divisor supported on that component is Cartier, which uses the characterisation of effective Cartier divisors and the local structure provided by the chapter's earlier results (source lines 4575-4590).

Expand the special fibre in its components: writing the divisor as a nonnegative combination of its irreducible components gives the displayed sum, the coefficients being the multiplicities, and the standard description of a sum of effective Cartier divisors as a union is quoted (source lines 4590-4598).

Identify the attached invertible sheaf as trivial: the sheaf attached to the special fibre is the structure sheaf because the divisor is principal, which is the last assertion of the statement and follows from the presentation of the sheaf attached to a principal divisor (source lines 4598-4604).

proof_roadmap.step: The uniformizer cuts the special fibre out as an effective Cartier divisor.
Each component is Cartier by the discrete valuation ring structure at its generic point.
Write the fibre as the sum of its components with the multiplicities as coefficients.
Conclude that the attached invertible sheaf is trivial.
